title: Machine Learning Essentials — authored transcript demo

segments.text: Supervised learning uses labeled examples to learn a mapping from inputs to outputs.
A training set is used to fit the model. A test set is held out to evaluate generalization on unseen examples.
Data leakage occurs when information unavailable at prediction time enters the training process.
Preprocessing should be fitted on training data only. A pipeline helps repeat preprocessing correctly inside each cross-validation fold.
Classification predicts discrete categories. Regression predicts numerical values.
Precision is the number of true positives divided by all predicted positives. High precision means fewer false alarms among positive predictions.
Recall is the number of true positives divided by all actual positives. High recall means fewer positive cases are missed.
For imbalanced datasets, accuracy can be misleading. A classifier that always predicts the majority class may have high accuracy but poor minority recall.
Overfitting means a model captures training-specific patterns that do not generalize. Regularization and suitable validation can reduce overfitting.
Cross-validation evaluates models across several training and validation splits. Hyperparameters should not be selected using the final test set.
A confusion matrix records true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives.
Model confidence is not a guarantee of correctness. Probability calibration compares predicted probabilities with observed frequencies.
A lower classification threshold usually increases recall and can increase false positives. Threshold selection should reflect the application and use validation data.
After deployment, changes in incoming data can reduce model performance. Monitoring and human feedback help identify these changes.
